card.name: A two‑storey cream‑brick colonial home with
card.summary: A two‑storey cream‑brick colonial home with a big front porch, blue entry door and red tiled roof.
card.description: The new two‑storey colonial residence occupies a 1300 × 1000 cm footprint and rises to a total height of 500 cm, capped by a striking red‑tile pitched roof that echoes early 20th‑century pattern‑book aesthetics. Cream‑colored brick walls, 20 cm thick, provide a solid, timeless envelope while a generous 400 cm deep front porch stretches across the entire façade, offering a welcoming transition from street to interior. A bold blue solid‑wood front door, 90 × 210 cm, is set centrally and swings on sturdy hinges, creating a vivid focal point against the muted cream. The house contains four spacious bedrooms and two full bathrooms, each served by a modern plumbing and electrical core that runs vertically through the reinforced concrete slab and rises through the interior walls. Interior partitions of drywall on timber studs define the living, dining, kitchen and study spaces, all finished with white plaster and hardwood flooring. A two‑car garage sits to the left, its steel roll‑up door matching the functional simplicity of the era. The porch is finished with treated timber decking, a protective over‑hang of asphalt shingles, and a wrought‑iron railing that adds both safety and decorative charm. Every element—from the red roof to the blue door—has been dimensioned to fit precisely within the overall envelope, ensuring a harmonious, build‑ready model.
plan: Measure the lot dimensions (1300 cm × 1000 cm) and confirm setbacks before staking the foundation layout.
Draft a full‑scale plan showing two storeys, a 400 cm deep front porch, a 90 × 210 cm blue entry door and a red‑tiled pitched roof.
Excavate and pour a reinforced concrete slab foundation 20 cm thick that matches the 1300 × 1000 cm footprint.
Erect load‑bearing brick walls to a height of 244 cm per story, installing window and door openings as per the plan.
Install floor joists, stair stringers, roof trusses, roofing, plumbing, electrical, HVAC and interior finishes, then fit the blue front door and porch railings.
Conduct a final inspection, verify that the red roof, blue door and big porch meet the design intent, and hand over the completed home.
assumptions: Because the brief gave no story count, the design adopts the typical two‑storey layout found in the Cronhardt and Cosgrove reference plans.
The number of bedrooms (four) and bathrooms (two) follows the common 7‑room configuration of 1920s pattern‑book homes.
Wall material is taken as brick with a cream finish, matching the Coloma bungalow’s brick construction and the colonial style of the Cronhardt.
A two‑car garage is provided as it appears in the Cosgrove design and is a standard amenity for modern suburban homes.
questions: Should the interior floor plan follow a specific historic layout (e.g., central hall versus side‑hall) or can it be a contemporary open‑plan arrangement?
Is there a preferred finish for the porch roof (e.g., continuation of the red tile or a different material) beyond the general description?
Do you require any special accessibility features such as a ramp to the front porch or a wider doorway?

card.name: A two‑storey white‑brick colonial home with
card.summary: A two‑storey white‑brick colonial home with a big porch, blue front door, red tiled roof, and complete kitchen and bathroom fixtures.
card.description: The new two‑storey colonial residence occupies a 12.80 m × 9.91 m footprint with 2.44 m ceiling heights on each level, presenting a dignified white brick façade crowned by a vivid red tiled roof. A generous front porch, 4 m deep and spanning the full width, invites arrival beneath a blue solid‑wood front door set in a traditional six‑panel frame with brass hinges. The porch roof overhang, clad in timber and shingle, provides shelter while echoing the building's historic proportions. Inside, the layout follows a classic seven‑room plan: a spacious living room, formal dining, a well‑appointed kitchen, and four bedrooms, complemented by two full bathrooms. The kitchen features a stainless‑steel refrigerator, gas stove, and deep sink, all set against sleek laminate cabinets, and a solid‑wood dining table for family meals. The master bath boasts a ceramic bathtub and a matching toilet, serviced by concealed PVC plumbing. Interior finishes include hardwood flooring throughout, painted wood exterior siding, and double‑hung aluminum‑frame windows that slide open. Staircases of timber tread connect the levels, while the structural system of reinforced concrete slab, timber joists, and brick load‑bearing walls ensures durability. The house reads as a stately yet welcoming presence on the street, its bold colour accents and proportioned volumes reflecting both tradition and contemporary livability.
plan: Measure the lot dimensions (1280 cm × 991 cm) and confirm setbacks before staking the foundation layout.
Excavate to a depth of 80 cm, pour a 20 cm thick reinforced concrete slab, and let it cure for seven days.
Erect the exterior brick walls to a height of 244 cm per story, installing lintels for the windows and doors.
Install floor joists and sub‑floor sheathing for both levels, then apply plywood decking for the roof.
Fit the red tile roof, attach flashing, and install ridge vents before sealing all penetrations.
Finish interior partitions, install the blue front door, windows, stairs, and all kitchen and bathroom fixtures, then conduct a final inspection.
assumptions: The house adopts the Cronhardt colonial layout of 2 storeys, 7 rooms, and 2 bathrooms as a typical reference.
Exterior walls are constructed of standard 20 cm thick brick finished in white paint, a common finish for 1920s pattern‑book homes.
The roof is assumed to be a pitched red clay‑tile roof, matching the brief’s colour request and typical of the era.
No garage is provided because the brief did not specify one; the footprint is fully allocated to living spaces and the large front porch.
questions: What is the desired overall width and depth of the front porch beyond the generic ‘big’ description?
Should the blue front door be a single panel or a double‑panel design, and does it include any sidelights?
Are there any specific interior style preferences (e.g., crown moulding, flooring type) that should be reflected beyond the basic fixtures listed?

card.name: A single‑storey, four‑room cottage with a
card.summary: A single‑storey, four‑room cottage with a 8 ft × 5 ft front porch, wood clapboard siding, and gabled roof.
card.description: The modest 1920s‑inspired cottage occupies a 22 ft × 40 ft (671 cm × 1219 cm) rectangular footprint with a single story rising to a 2.44 m ceiling. Its exterior is clad in traditional white‑painted wood clapboard, echoing the quiet charm of lake‑side homes. Four well‑proportioned rooms—two bedrooms, a living area, and a kitchen—share a central hallway that leads to a compact bathroom. A gabled roof of asphalt shingles caps the structure, while timber roof trusses provide a modest pitch. The front porch, precisely eight feet wide (244 cm) and five feet deep (152 cm), projects from the façade, supported by timber decking and a simple railing, offering a welcoming threshold. The front door, a solid wood panel on a hinge, opens onto the porch, and four double‑hung windows slide to admit daylight. Interior finishes include plasterboard walls, wood trim, and modest cabinetry. All structural elements rest on a 15 cm thick concrete slab foundation, ensuring durability. The design balances historic modesty with contemporary comfort, delivering a functional, aesthetically pleasing home for a small family.
plan: Measure the lot dimensions and verify the 8 ft (244 cm) wide by 5 ft (152 cm) deep porch footprint fits within the 22 ft × 40 ft (671 cm × 1219 cm) house envelope.
Draft a single‑storey floor plan showing four rooms, one bathroom, and the front porch placement using 2.44 m ceiling heights.
Consult structural engineers to size foundation slabs, floor joists, and roof trusses for the 671 cm × 1219 cm footprint.
Order all timber, concrete, siding, roofing, and finish materials according to the bill of quantities.
Coordinate trades – excavators pour the concrete slab, framers erect walls and roof, carpenters install porch decking and railings, and finish carpenters fit doors, windows, and interior trim.
Finish interior finishes, install fixtures, conduct a final inspection, and certify the home as complete.
assumptions: The house follows the Mineola pattern: one storey, four rooms, one bathroom, and a simple front porch.
Wall material is wood and painted white, a common finish for 1920s pattern‑book homes.
The roof is a gabled design with asphalt shingles, matching typical construction of the era.
No garage is provided, as the brief does not mention one and the reference designs omit it.
questions: What roof pitch and over‑hang dimensions are desired for the gabled roof?
How many and what sizes of windows are required on each façade?
Would you like any interior style details (e.g., crown molding, flooring type) beyond the basic layout?
